rows.title: Buy or licence one historical price archive
rows.detail: One licensed archive with a stated open/close timestamp would convert most of this site's blanks into numbers. Nothing else on this list unlocks as much.
rows.risk: A cheap archive with no timestamp flag would be worse than none: it cannot be labelled open vs close, so every CLV claim stays invalid.
rows.decision: Approve a budget and a vendor shortlist.

rows.title: Run the capture schedule that already exists
rows.detail: The capture script is written. Pointing a scheduled job at the official report on Wed/Thu/Fri and at kickoff-minus-60 costs almost nothing and creates the series every availability feature needs.
rows.risk: A capture that overwrites rather than appends destroys the series. The store must stay immutable per observation.

rows.title: Capture official inactive lists per game
rows.detail: The single biggest evidence gap in the availability work. Without inactive lists a listed player cannot be confirmed absent, so a replacement is suspected and never established.
rows.cost: Medium (a source + a parser + a daily schedule)
rows.risk: An inactive list captured after the game is not point-in-time and cannot be used for a backtest.
rows.decision: Approve the source and the capture window.

rows.title: Add a second price observation within 24 hours
rows.detail: Even a second capture from the same community release would turn one snapshot into an interval and let the ledger distinguish an open from a close for the unplayed Week 10 games.
rows.risk: Two captures of the same number prove nothing about movement. The value is purely in establishing the pipeline.
rows.decision: Approve running the capture twice a day.

rows.title: Pin row counts and field sets per source, and alert on a miss
rows.detail: The build already fails closed on a reconciliation break. Extending that to per-source row counts turns a silent blank into a loud failure.
rows.risk: A brittle pin can fail on legitimate news (a club adding a player). Set the bound as a band, not an exact count.

rows.title: Publish a per-team deficiency page with both sides of the ball
rows.detail: The current deficiency view is offense-side, because that is what the report designates. A defensive view needs the opposing club's chart, which exists for 30 clubs.
rows.cost: Medium (a join across two club charts)
rows.risk: Joining two different clubs' charts invites a positional mismatch that looks like a deficiency but is only a naming difference.
rows.decision: Approve the cross-club join with a published position map.
rows.source_label: NFL injury report (OFFICIAL); club charts captured in decision-lab/data/official_snapshot.json

rows.title: Fund the sample, not the model
rows.detail: Every scored rule is within noise. More modelling effort on 137 games will produce a better-looking number, not a better number. The cheapest path to a decision is more graded legs at fixed, pre-registered rules.
rows.cost: Low in money, high in patience
rows.risk: Re-using this corpus with new rules inflates the multiplicity problem; new legs must be genuinely out of sample.
rows.decision: Approve a fixed evaluation window and no rule changes inside it.

rows.title: Make the demotion rule binding on the owner, not just the build
rows.detail: Two rules have already failed their kill condition. A leaderboard that demotes but never acts is a dashboard, not a governance system.
rows.risk: Demoting aggressively can bury a rule that needed one more week. The kill condition is therefore pre-registered, not discretionary.
rows.decision: Approve that a demoted rule needs a new hash to return.

rows.title: State the reuse position before adding more captures
rows.detail: The repository stores private captures and publishes derived analysis. That is a defensible position only if it is written down per source class.
rows.risk: Publishing a raw row from a source whose terms forbid it would compromise every page that cites it.
rows.decision: Approve the public/private split in writing.
